paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the empirical generalization errors (RTE) in relation to different ranks used for fine-tuning language models with QAdapter on Llama-3-8B. The x-axis is labeled "Rank," representing discrete rank values of 4, 16, 64, and 256, and employs a linear scale with intervals set according to these values. The y-axis, labeled "Errors (RTE)," represents the error rate, ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, and is also on a linear scale with relevant tick labels. 

There are five data points indicated by green circles, connected by a solid black line. The first data point at rank 4 has an error value of 0.3, and subsequent points are at 0.3 for rank 16, 0.31 for rank 64, and 0.6 for rank 256. The error shows a relatively stable trend at lower ranks, followed by a noticeable increase at rank 256. Each green circle includes vertical error bars that depict variability in error around each mean value, highlighting the range of generalization errors associated with each rank.
